newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strike over at UPS Rennes centre.
newsitem.headline: Strike over at UPS Rennes centre.

text.p: A strike by around 40 staff working at United Parcel Service French centre, at Rennes, in western France, ended Wednesday evening, a company official told Reuters.
"The strike, which lasted 48 hours, is now over and personnel and management have reached common ground on a number of points which will be discussed at a works council meeting next month."

The strike had been sparked by union claims that UPS planned to transfer and close certain activities at Rennes such as those concerning the transport of heavyweight shipments, chartering and warehousing, as part of a strategy to recentre its business on documents and small parcels.

"Our back-up plans ensured that was no disruption to traffic while our weekday air cargo feeder service between the Paris/CDG hub and Rennes operated normally during the strike," the UPS official said

In June 1996, strike action hit several of UPS France' centres with personnel protesting at company restructuring and its redundancy programme. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
